sanskrit: hatān parivahantaś ca yantritāḥ paramāyudhaiḥ diśo jagmur mahānāgāḥ ke cid ekacarā iva
english: Bearing away the slain and held fast by the finest weapons, the great elephants scattered to every quarter, some wandering off alone as though solitary beasts.

sanskrit: tāḍitās tāḍyamānāś ca tomararṣṭiparaśvadhaiḥ petur ārtasvaraṃ kṛtvā tadā viśasane gajāḥ
english: Struck and struck again by lances, spears, and battle-axes, the elephants fell with cries of anguish there amid the slaughter.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ śailopamaiḥ kāyair nipatadbhiḥ samantataḥ āhatā sahasā bhūmiś cakampe ca nanāda ca
english: As their mountain-like bodies came crashing down on every side, the earth, struck all at once, both trembled and resounded.

sanskrit: sāditaiḥ sagajārohaiḥ sapatākaiḥ samantataḥ mātaṅgaiḥ śuśubhe bhūmir vikīrṇair iva parvataiḥ
english: With elephants brought low on every side, their riders and banners with them, the ground shone as if strewn with scattered mountains.

sanskrit: gajasthāś ca mahāmātrā nirbhinnahṛdayā raṇe rathibhiḥ pātitā bhallair vikīrṇāṅkuśatomarāḥ
english: The mahouts upon the elephants, their hearts pierced through in battle, were felled by the chariot-warriors' broad-headed shafts, their goads and lances flung about.

sanskrit: krauñcavad vinadanto 'nye nārācābhihatā gajāḥ parān svāṃś cāpi mṛdnantaḥ paripetur diśo daśa
english: Other elephants, smitten by iron arrows, trumpeting like cranes, fled crashing through the ten directions, trampling enemy and friend alike.

sanskrit: gajāśvarathasaṃghānāṃ śarīraughasamāvṛtā babhūva pṛthivī rājan māṃsaśoṇitakardamā
english: Covered with the heaped bodies of hosts of elephants, horses, and chariots, the earth, O king, became a mire of flesh and blood.

sanskrit: pramathya ca viṣāṇāgraiḥ samutkṣipya ca vāraṇaiḥ sacakrāś ca vicakrāś ca rathair eva mahārathāḥ
english: Crushed and tossed aloft by the elephants' tusk-tips, the great chariot-warriors, with their cars whole or with wheels torn away, lay strewn upon the field.

sanskrit: rathāś ca rathibhir hīnā nirmanuṣyāś ca vājinaḥ hatārohāś ca mātaṅgā diśo jagmuḥ śarāturāḥ
english: Chariots bereft of their warriors, horses bereft of their men, and elephants whose riders were slain fled to every quarter, tormented by arrows.

sanskrit: jaghānātra pitā putraṃ putraś ca pitaraṃ tathā ity āsīt tumulaṃ yuddhaṃ na prajñāyata kiṃ cana
english: There a father slew his son and a son his father; so tumultuous was the battle that nothing whatever could be discerned.

sanskrit: ā gulphebhyo 'vasīdanta narāḥ śoṇitakardame dīpyamānaiḥ parikṣiptā dāvair iva mahādrumāḥ
english: Men sank to their ankles in the mire of blood, hemmed in as great trees encircled by blazing forest fires.

sanskrit: śoṇitaiḥ sicyamānāni vastrāṇi kavacāni ca chatrāṇi ca patākāś ca sarvaṃ raktam adṛśyata
english: Garments and armor, parasols and banners, all drenched with blood, appeared crimson to the eye.

sanskrit: hayaughāś ca rathaughāś ca naraughāś ca nipātitāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ punar āvṛttā bahudhā rathanemibhiḥ
english: Multitudes of horses, of chariots, and of men, struck down, were rolled over and over again and ground in many ways by the chariot-wheels.

sanskrit: sa gajaughamahāvegaḥ parāsunaraśaivalaḥ rathaughatumulāvartaḥ prababhau sainyasāgaraḥ
english: That ocean of armies shone forth, its great surge the throng of elephants, its waterweed the lifeless men, its turbulent whirlpools the masses of chariots.

sanskrit: taṃ vāhanamahānaubhir yodhā jayadhanaiṣiṇaḥ avagāhyāvamajjanto naiva mohaṃ pracakrire
english: Plunging into it with their mounts for great ships, the warriors who craved the wealth of victory, though sinking down, gave way to no bewilderment.

sanskrit: śaravarṣābhivṛṣṭeṣu yodheṣv ajitalakṣmasu na hi svacittatāṃ lebhe kaś cid āhatalakṣaṇaḥ
english: Among the warriors rained upon by showers of arrows, their tokens of valor not yet won, not one who bore the marks of wounds could keep his own composure.

sanskrit: vartamāne tathā yuddhe ghorarūpe bhayaṃkare mohayitvā parān droṇo yudhiṣṭhiram upādravat
english: As that battle, terrible of aspect and dreadful, raged on, Droṇa, having confounded the foe, rushed upon Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tato yudhiṣṭhiro droṇaṃ dṛṣṭvāntikam upāgatam mahatā śaravarṣeṇa pratyagṛhṇād abhītavat
english: Saṃjaya said: Then Yudhiṣṭhira, seeing Droṇa drawn near, received him fearlessly with a great shower of arrows.

sanskrit: tato halahalāśabda āsīd yaudhiṣṭhire bale jighṛkṣati mahāsiṃhe gajānām iva yūthapam
english: Then a tumultuous din arose within Yudhiṣṭhira's host, as when a great lion seeks to seize the leader of a herd of elephants.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā droṇaṃ tataḥ śūraḥ satyajit satyavikramaḥ yudhiṣṭhiraṃ pariprepsum ācāryaṃ samupādravat
english: Seeing Droṇa bent on reaching Yudhiṣṭhira, the hero Satyajit, of truthful valor, then rushed upon the teacher.

sanskrit: tata ācāryapāñcālyau yuyudhāte parasparam vikṣobhayantau tat sainyam indravairocanāv iva
english: Then the teacher and the Pāñcāla fought one another, throwing that army into turmoil like Indra and the son of Virocana of old.

sanskrit: tataḥ satyajitaṃ tīkṣṇair daśabhir marmabhedibhiḥ avidhyac chīghram ācāryaś chittvāsya saśaraṃ dhanuḥ
english: Then the teacher swiftly pierced Satyajit with ten keen, vital-rending shafts, cutting away his bow with its arrow set.

sanskrit: sa śīghrataram ādāya dhanur anyat pratāpavān droṇaṃ so 'bhijaghānāśu viṃśadbhiḥ kaṅkapatribhiḥ
english: Taking up another bow more swiftly still, the valiant warrior at once struck Droṇa with twenty heron-feathered arrows.

sanskrit: jñātvā satyajitā droṇaṃ grasyamānam ivāhave vṛkaḥ śaraśatais tīkṣṇaiḥ pāñcālyo droṇam ardayat
english: Seeing Droṇa as if devoured by Satyajit in the fight, the Pāñcāla Vṛka harried Droṇa with hundreds of keen arrows.

sanskrit: saṃchādyamānaṃ samare droṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahāratham cukruśuḥ pāṇḍavā rājan vastrāṇi dudhuvuś ca ha
english: Beholding the great chariot-warrior Droṇa overwhelmed in the fight, the Pāṇḍavas raised a shout, O king, and waved their garments aloft.

sanskrit: vṛkas tu paramakruddho droṇaṃ ṣaṣṭyā stanāntare vivyādha balavān rājaṃs tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: And the mighty Vṛka, in utmost wrath, pierced Droṇa between the breasts with sixty shafts, O king; and that seemed a marvel.

sanskrit: droṇas tu śaravarṣeṇa chādyamāno mahārathaḥ vegaṃ cakre mahāvegaḥ krodhād udvṛtya cakṣuṣī
english: But the great chariot-warrior Droṇa, that mighty force, overspread by the shower of arrows, gathered his speed, his eyes rolling with wrath.

sanskrit: tataḥ satyajitaś cāpaṃ chittvā droṇo vṛkasya ca ṣaḍbhiḥ sasūtaṃ sahayaṃ śarair droṇo 'vadhīd vṛkam
english: Then Droṇa cut away the bows of both Satyajit and Vṛka, and with six arrows Droṇa slew Vṛka together with his charioteer and horses.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya satyajid vegavattaram sāśvaṃ sasūtaṃ viśikhair droṇaṃ vivyādha sadhvajam
english: Then Satyajit, taking up another swifter bow, pierced Droṇa with his horses, charioteer, and banner, with shafts.

sanskrit: sa tan na mamṛṣe droṇaḥ pāñcālyenārdanaṃ mṛdhe tatas tasya vināśāya satvaraṃ vyasṛjac charān
english: Droṇa could not brook this harrying by the Pāñcāla in the fray; so for his destruction he loosed his arrows in haste.

sanskrit: hayān dhvajaṃ dhanur muṣṭim ubhau ca pārṣṇisārathī avākirat tato droṇaḥ śaravarṣaiḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: His horses, his banner, the grip of his bow, and both his flanking charioteers—all these Droṇa then overwhelmed with showers of arrows by the thousand.

sanskrit: tathā saṃchidyamāneṣu kārmukeṣu punaḥ punaḥ pāñcālyaḥ paramāstrajñaḥ śoṇāśvaṃ samayodhayat
english: Though his bows were cut to pieces again and again, the Pāñcāla, supreme master of weapons, kept battling him whose horses were red.

sanskrit: sa satyajitam ālakṣya tathodīrṇaṃ mahāhave ardhacandreṇa ciccheda śiras tasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Marking Satyajit risen up so in the great battle, Droṇa with a crescent-headed shaft severed the head of that noble man.

sanskrit: tasmin hate mahāmātre pāñcālānāṃ ratharṣabhe apāyāj javanair aśvair droṇāt trasto yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: When that mighty bull among the chariot-warriors of the Pāñcālas was slain, Yudhiṣṭhira, in dread of Droṇa, withdrew on his swift horses.

sanskrit: pāñcālāḥ kekayā matsyāś cedikārūṣakosalāḥ yudhiṣṭhiram udīkṣanto hṛṣṭā droṇam upādravan
english: The Pāñcālas, Kekayas, Matsyas, Cedis, Kārūṣas, and Kosalas, looking to Yudhiṣṭhira, joyfully rushed upon Droṇa.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiraprepsur ācāryaḥ śatrupūgahā vyadhamat tāny anīkāni tūlarāśim ivānilaḥ
english: Then the teacher, slayer of throngs of foes, eager to reach Yudhiṣṭhira, scattered those battalions as the wind scatters a heap of cotton.

sanskrit: nirdahantam anīkāni tāni tāni punaḥ punaḥ droṇaṃ matsyād avarajaḥ śatānīko 'bhyavartata
english: As Droṇa burned through those battalions again and again, Śatānīka, younger brother of the Matsya king, advanced against him.

sanskrit: sūryaraśmipratīkāśaiḥ karmāraparimārjitaiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ sasūtaṃ sahayaṃ droṇaṃ viddhvānadad bhṛśam
english: With six arrows bright as the sun's rays and burnished by the smith, he pierced Droṇa together with his charioteer and horses, and roared aloud.

sanskrit: tasya nānadato droṇaḥ śiraḥ kāyāt sakuṇḍalam kṣureṇāpāharat tūrṇaṃ tato matsyāḥ pradudruvuḥ
english: As he roared, Droṇa with a razor-headed shaft swiftly struck his head, with its earrings, from his body; and thereupon the Matsyas fled.

sanskrit: matsyāñ jitvājayac cedīn kārūṣān kekayān api pāñcālān sṛñjayān pāṇḍūn bhāradvājaḥ punaḥ punaḥ
english: Having vanquished the Matsyas, the son of Bharadvāja conquered the Cedis, the Kārūṣas, the Kekayas, the Pāñcālas, the Sṛñjayas, and the Pāṇḍus, again and again.

sanskrit: taṃ dahantam anīkāni kruddham agniṃ yathā vanam dṛṣṭvā rukmarathaṃ kruddhaṃ samakampanta sṛñjayāḥ
english: Seeing him of the golden chariot, wrathful, consuming the battalions like a raging fire a forest, the Sṛñjayas trembled.

sanskrit: uttamaṃ hy ādadhānasya dhanur asyāśukāriṇaḥ jyāghoṣo nighnato 'mitrān dikṣu sarvāsu śuśruve
english: As that swift-handed one drew his peerless bow and struck down his foes, the twang of his bowstring was heard in all the quarters.

sanskrit: nāgān aśvān padātīṃś ca rathino gajasādinaḥ raudrā hastavatā muktāḥ pramathnanti sma sāyakāḥ
english: Elephants, horses, and foot-soldiers, chariot-warriors and elephant-riders—the dreadful arrows loosed by that deft hand crushed them all.

sanskrit: nānadyamānaḥ parjanyo miśravāto himātyaye aśmavarṣam ivāvarṣat pareṣāṃ bhayam ādadhat
english: Like a thundering rain-cloud mingled with wind at winter's end, he rained down what seemed a hail of stones, striking terror into the foe.

sanskrit: sarvā diśaḥ samacarat sainyaṃ vikṣobhayann iva balī śūro maheṣvāso mitrāṇām abhayaṃkaraḥ
english: That mighty hero, the great archer, giver of safety to his friends, ranged over all the quarters as though convulsing the host.

sanskrit: tasya vidyud ivābhreṣu cāpaṃ hemapariṣkṛtam dikṣu sarvāsv apaśyāma droṇasyāmitatejasaḥ
english: Like lightning amid the clouds, we beheld in every quarter the gold-adorned bow of Droṇa of boundless splendor.

sanskrit: droṇas tu pāṇḍavānīke cakāra kadanaṃ mahat yathā daityagaṇe viṣṇuḥ surāsuranamaskṛtaḥ
english: And Droṇa wrought great havoc in the Pāṇḍava host, as Viṣṇu, honored by gods and demons alike, once did among the throngs of the Daityas.

sanskrit: sa śūraḥ satyavāk prājño balavān satyavikramaḥ mahānubhāvaḥ kālānte raudrīṃ bhīruvibhīṣaṇām
english: That hero, truthful in speech, wise, mighty, of true valor, and of great majesty—at the end of time, dreadful and terrifying to the timid—

sanskrit: kavacormidhvajāvartāṃ martyakūlāpahāriṇīm gajavājimahāgrāhām asimīnāṃ durāsadām
english: a river whose waves were coats of mail and whose whirlpools were banners, sweeping away the banks of mortal men, with elephants and horses for its great crocodiles, swords for its fish, hard to cross,

sanskrit: vīrāsthiśarkarāṃ raudrāṃ bherīmurajakacchapām carmavarmaplavāṃ ghorāṃ keśaśaivalaśāḍvalām
english: with the bones of heroes for its gravel, dreadful, with kettledrums and tabors for its turtles, with shields and armor for its rafts, terrible, with hair for its waterweed and water-grass,

sanskrit: śaraughiṇīṃ dhanuḥsrotāṃ bāhupannagasaṃkulām raṇabhūmivahāṃ ghorāṃ kurusṛñjayavāhinīm manuṣyaśīrṣapāṣāṇāṃ śaktimīnāṃ gadoḍupām
english: running with floods of arrows, its currents bows, thronged with arms for serpents, the dread stream that the battlefield bore along, the river of the Kurus and Sṛñjayas, with men's heads for stones, spears for fish, and maces for its boats,

sanskrit: uṣṇīṣaphenavasanāṃ niṣkīrṇāntrasarīsṛpām vīrāpahāriṇīm ugrāṃ māṃsaśoṇitakardamām
english: with turbans for its foam and raiment, with spilled entrails for its crawling reptiles, fierce, bearing away heroes, terrible, its mire of flesh and blood,

sanskrit: hastigrāhāṃ ketuvṛkṣāṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ nimajjanīm krūrāṃ śarīrasaṃghāṭāṃ sādinakrāṃ duratyayām droṇaḥ prāvartayat tatra nadīm antakagāminīm
english: with elephants for its alligators and banners for its trees, drowning the warriors, cruel, with heaped bodies for its rafts and cavalrymen for its crocodiles, impassable—such a river, flowing to the realm of Death, did Droṇa set coursing there.

sanskrit: kravyādagaṇasaṃghuṣṭāṃ śvaśṛgālagaṇāyutām niṣevitāṃ mahāraudraiḥ piśitāśaiḥ samantataḥ
english: It rang with the cries of flesh-eating throngs, swarmed with packs of dogs and jackals, and was haunted on every side by the most dreadful devourers of carrion.

sanskrit: taṃ dahantam anīkāni rathodāraṃ kṛtāntavat sarvato 'bhyadravan droṇaṃ kuntīputrapurogamāḥ
english: As that lordly chariot-warrior, like Death itself, burned through their battalions, the sons of Kuntī at their head rushed upon Droṇa from every side.

sanskrit: tāṃs tu śūrān maheṣvāsāṃs tāvakābhyudyatāyudhāḥ rājāno rājaputrāś ca samantāt paryavārayan
english: But your kings and princes, their weapons raised, surrounded those heroic great archers on every side.

sanskrit: tato droṇaḥ satyasaṃdhaḥ prabhinna iva kuñjaraḥ abhyatītya rathānīkaṃ dṛḍhasenam apātayat
english: Then Droṇa, true to his word, like an elephant in rut, broke through the chariot-ranks and brought down Dṛḍhasena.

sanskrit: tato rājānam āsādya praharantam abhītavat avidhyan navabhiḥ kṣemaṃ sa hataḥ prāpatad rathāt
english: Then, falling upon king Kṣema as he struck fearlessly, he pierced him with nine arrows; and Kṣema, slain, dropped from his chariot.

sanskrit: sa madhyaṃ prāpya sainyānāṃ sarvāḥ pravicaran diśaḥ trātā hy abhavad anyeṣāṃ na trātavyaḥ kathaṃ cana
english: Reaching the midst of the armies and ranging through all the quarters, he became the protector of others, while he himself could in no way be brought to bay.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍinaṃ dvādaśabhir viṃśatyā cottamaujasam vasudānaṃ ca bhallena preṣayad yamasādanam
english: With twelve arrows he struck Śikhaṇḍin, with twenty Uttamaujas, and with a broad-headed shaft he sent Vasudāna to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: aśītyā kṣatravarmāṇaṃ ṣaḍviṃśatyā sudakṣiṇam kṣatradevaṃ tu bhallena rathanīḍād apāharat
english: With eighty arrows he pierced Kṣatravarman, with twenty-six Sudakṣiṇa, and with a broad-headed shaft he struck Kṣatradeva from the seat of his chariot.

sanskrit: yudhāmanyuṃ catuḥṣaṣṭyā triṃśatā caiva sātyakim viddhvā rukmarathas tūrṇaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram upādravat
english: Having pierced Yudhāmanyu with sixty-four arrows and Sātyaki with thirty, he of the golden chariot swiftly rushed upon Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiraḥ kṣipraṃ kitavo rājasattamaḥ apāyāj javanair aśvaiḥ pāñcālyo droṇam abhyayāt
english: Then Yudhiṣṭhira, best of kings, withdrew at once on his swift horses; and Kitava the Pāñcāla advanced against Droṇa.

sanskrit: taṃ droṇaḥ sadhanuṣkaṃ tu sāśvayantāram akṣiṇot sa hataḥ prāpatad bhūmau rathāj jyotir ivāmbarāt
english: Droṇa struck him down together with his bow, his horses, and his driver; and slain, he fell to the ground from his chariot, like a star from the sky.

sanskrit: tasmin hate rājaputre pāñcālānāṃ yaśaskare hata droṇaṃ hata droṇam ity āsīt tumulaṃ mahat
english: When that prince, the glory of the Pāñcālas, was slain, a great tumult arose: "Slay Droṇa! Slay Droṇa!"

sanskrit: tāṃs tathā bhṛśasaṃkruddhān pāñcālān matsyakekayān sṛñjayān pāṇḍavāṃś caiva droṇo vyakṣobhayad balī
english: The mighty Droṇa threw into disorder those furiously enraged Pāñcālas, Matsyas, Kekayas, Sṛñjayas, and Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: sātyakiṃ cekitānaṃ ca dhṛṣṭadyumnaśikhaṇḍinau vārdhakṣemiṃ citrasenaṃ senābinduṃ suvarcasam
english: Sātyaki and Cekitāna, Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Śikhaṇḍin, Vārdhakṣemi, Citrasena, Senābindu, and Suvarcas—

sanskrit: etāṃś cānyāṃś ca subahūn nānājanapadeśvarān sarvān droṇo 'jayad yuddhe kurubhiḥ parivāritaḥ
english: these and many others besides, lords of various realms, all of them Droṇa vanquished in battle, surrounded by the Kurus.

sanskrit: tāvakās tu mahārāja jayaṃ labdhvā mahāhave pāṇḍaveyān raṇe jaghnur dravamāṇān samantataḥ
english: And your men, O great king, having won victory in that mighty battle, slew the Pāṇḍava forces as they fled in all directions.

sanskrit: te dānavā ivendreṇa vadhyamānā mahātmanā pāñcālāḥ kekayā matsyāḥ samakampanta bhārata
english: Slain by the great-souled Droṇa as the Dānavas were once slain by Indra, the Pāñcālas, Kekayas, and Matsyas trembled, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca bhāradvājena bhagneṣu pāṇḍaveṣu mahāmṛdhe pāñcāleṣu ca sarveṣu kaś cid anyo 'bhyavartata
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When the Pāṇḍavas and all the Pāñcālas were broken by the son of Bharadvāja in that great battle, did any other turn back to face him,

sanskrit: āryāṃ yuddhe matiṃ kṛtvā kṣatriyāṇāṃ yaśaskarīm asevitāṃ kāpuruṣaiḥ sevitāṃ puruṣarṣabhaiḥ
english: having set his mind in battle upon the noble resolve that brings the warrior fame—shunned by cowards, embraced by bulls among men?

sanskrit: sa hi vīro naraḥ sūta yo bhagneṣu nivartate aho nāsīt pumān kaś cid dṛṣṭvā droṇaṃ vyavasthitam
english: For that man, O charioteer, is a hero who turns back when others are routed. Alas, was there not a single man who stood firm at the sight of Droṇa,

sanskrit: jṛmbhamāṇam iva vyāghraṃ prabhinnam iva kuñjaram tyajantam āhave prāṇān saṃnaddhaṃ citrayodhinam
english: who, like a yawning tiger, like an elephant in rut, laying down his very life in battle, stood armed and skilled in varied modes of warfare,

sanskrit: maheṣvāsaṃ naravyāghraṃ dviṣatām aghavardhanam kṛtajñaṃ satyanirataṃ duryodhanahitaiṣiṇam
english: the great archer, that tiger among men, who multiplied the woes of his foes, grateful, devoted to truth, seeker of Duryodhana's good?

sanskrit: bhāradvājaṃ tathānīke dṛṣṭvā śūram avasthitam ke vīrāḥ saṃnyavartanta tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: Seeing the son of Bharadvāja, that hero, thus standing firm in the front of battle, which heroes turned back to meet him? Tell me that, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tān dṛṣṭvā calitān saṃkhye praṇunnān droṇasāyakaiḥ pāñcālān pāṇḍavān matsyān sṛñjayāṃś cedikekayān
english: Saṃjaya said: Seeing them shaken in the fray and driven off by Droṇa's arrows—the Pāñcālas, Pāṇḍavas, Matsyas, Sṛñjayas, Cedis, and Kekayas—

sanskrit: droṇacāpavimuktena śaraugheṇāsuhāriṇā sindhor iva mahaughena hriyamāṇān yathā plavān
english: borne away by the life-stealing flood of arrows loosed from Droṇa's bow, like rafts swept off by the great current of a river,

sanskrit: kauravāḥ siṃhanādena nānāvādyasvanena ca rathadvipanarāśvaiś ca sarvataḥ paryavārayan
english: the Kauravas, with lions' roars and the din of many instruments, with chariots, elephants, men, and horses, surrounded them on every side.

sanskrit: tān paśyan sainyamadhyastho rājā svajanasaṃvṛtaḥ duryodhano 'bravīt karṇaṃ prahṛṣṭaḥ prahasann iva
english: Beholding them, king Duryodhana, standing in the midst of his host and surrounded by his kinsmen, in high delight and as if laughing, spoke to Karṇa.
